A.title: Regional Office Site Selection
A.instructions: Review the general information below together with your group. Then read your own private report -- it contains additional information that only you have received. Discuss the three candidate locations with your group, and be ready to record your own individual decision both before and after the discussion.

generalInfo.text: TechNova Analytics, a mid-size data-analytics firm, needs to open a new regional office within the next 6 months to accommodate roughly 40 staff. A site-selection committee has shortlisted three candidate buildings: Rivermill Center, Oak Hollow Business Park, and Fenwick Crossing Tower.
All three buildings currently have 8,000-10,000 square feet available and have confirmed availability within TechNova's required move-in window.
Rivermill Center's publicly listed monthly rent is $18,000.
Oak Hollow Business Park's publicly listed monthly rent is $21,000.
Fenwick Crossing Tower's publicly listed monthly rent is $19,500.

options.label: Rivermill Center
options.description: A mid-rise office building near the downtown core with the lowest publicly listed rent of the three candidates.

options.label: Oak Hollow Business Park
options.description: A suburban office park with the highest publicly listed rent of the three candidates.

options.label: Fenwick Crossing Tower
options.description: A newer tower with a mid-range publicly listed rent.

correctAnswer.rationale: Shared information alone highlights only headline rent, where Rivermill Center appears cheapest. Once all three private reports are pooled, Oak Hollow Business Park is the only option with no serious drawback in any of the three reviewed areas (logistics, true lease cost, and growth/transit), while Rivermill Center's low headline rent is offset by a large signing fee and steep annual increases (A2-E1), congested shared parking and elevator waits (A1-E1), and poor transit access with no room to grow (A3-E1). Fenwick Crossing Tower avoids Rivermill's cost problems but has its own move-in delay (A1-E3) and lacks nearby amenities and expansion space (A3-E3). Oak Hollow is the only option positively supported across all three private reports (A1-E2, A2-E2, A3-E2).

content.text: Rivermill Center has only one elevator serving all six floors, and tenants in the building report frequent wait times during peak hours. Its parking garage is shared with an adjacent shopping mall, and TechNova's facilities contact was told parking shortages are common on weekday afternoons.
Oak Hollow Business Park has a dedicated two-elevator bank serving its floors, and its on-site parking garage is reserved exclusively for office tenants, currently at about 60% capacity.

Fenwick Crossing Tower's available space has a non-standard floor plan that would require substantial build-out before move-in, adding an estimated 10 weeks to the timeline. The building has bike storage but no dedicated car parking; the nearest public garage is a 12-minute walk away.

Although Rivermill Center's listed rent is the lowest, its lease requires a one-time $45,000 building-improvement fee due at signing, and annual rent increases are set at 6% -- the highest of the three buildings.
Oak Hollow Business Park's lease has no signing fee, caps annual rent increases at 2.5%, and the landlord is currently offering two months of free rent as a move-in incentive.
Fenwick Crossing Tower's lease has no signing fee and standard annual rent increases of 4%, with no special incentives currently offered.

Rivermill Center's neighborhood has limited public transit, served by a single bus line whose last departure is 7pm; several current TechNova staff who were surveyed flagged this as a commute concern. The building has no additional space available if TechNova needs to expand.
Oak Hollow Business Park is within a 5-minute walk of two subway lines. The building also has an additional half-floor available for lease if TechNova grows beyond 40 staff within the next two years.

Fenwick Crossing Tower has decent bus access, but the surrounding neighborhood has no full-service restaurants within walking distance; a recent staff survey flagged lunch options as a concern. The building has no additional space available for future growth.

B.title: Fundraising Gala Caterer Selection
B.instructions: Review the general information below together with your group. Then read your own private report -- it contains additional information that only you have received. Discuss the three candidate caterers with your group, and be ready to record your own individual decision both before and after the discussion.

generalInfo.text: Bright Path Youth Foundation is planning its annual fundraising gala for approximately 150 guests. The event committee has shortlisted three catering vendors: Silver Fork Catering, Meridian Table, and Harborlight Catering.
All three vendors have catered nonprofit events of a similar size before and have confirmed availability on the gala date.
Silver Fork Catering's quoted price is $85 per guest.
Meridian Table's quoted price is $95 per guest.
Harborlight Catering's quoted price is $90 per guest.

options.label: Silver Fork Catering
options.description: The lowest quoted per-guest price of the three vendors.

options.label: Meridian Table
options.description: The highest quoted per-guest price of the three vendors.

correctAnswer.rationale: Shared information alone highlights only the quoted per-guest price, where Silver Fork Catering appears cheapest. Once all three private reports are pooled, Meridian Table is the only vendor with no serious drawback in any of the three reviewed areas (menu/dietary accommodation, logistics reliability, and true contract cost), while Silver Fork's low quote is offset by a mandatory service fee, gratuity, and travel surcharge that push its real per-guest cost above Meridian's (B3-E1), a documented history of late starts and a loading-dock conflict (B2-E1), and weak dietary accommodation (B1-E1). Harborlight avoids Silver Fork's worst cost problems but still adds a service fee (B3-E3), has a recent late-start incident (B2-E3), and offers limited dietary flexibility (B1-E3). Meridian Table is the only vendor positively supported across all three private reports (B1-E2, B2-E2, B3-E2).

content.text: Silver Fork Catering offers a single set menu with only one vegetarian option and no vegan substitution, and does not have a dedicated allergy-safe prep area.
Meridian Table offers a fully customizable menu, including three vegetarian and vegan options, and prepares allergy-sensitive dishes in a certified separate station.
Harborlight Catering offers one vegetarian dish and no vegan option; menu substitution requests must be submitted at least 30 days in advance and are not guaranteed.

Silver Fork Catering requires 4 hours of loading-dock access before the event, which conflicts with Bright Path's venue's restricted loading-dock hours. Two reference checks from prior nonprofit events both reported a 30-45 minute late start.
Meridian Table needs a 2-hour setup window that fits within the venue's loading-dock hours. Two independent reference checks covering the past three years reported zero late-start incidents.
Harborlight Catering needs a standard 3-hour setup window that fits the venue's hours. One reference check from a recent event reported a late start.

Silver Fork Catering's $85 quote excludes an 8% service fee and an 18% mandatory gratuity added afterward, plus a $500 travel surcharge because Bright Path's venue is outside their home service district.
Meridian Table's $95 quote is fully inclusive of service fee and gratuity, with no travel surcharge regardless of venue location.
Harborlight Catering's $90 quote excludes a 10% service fee; gratuity is optional and not required. There is no travel surcharge.
